lesson.title: 3.7 What language do you speak?
lesson.unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
lesson.unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
lesson.goal: Ask and say which languages people speak (What language do you speak? I speak Spanish and English.).
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.7 Where Are You From?: A1 asks where people are from (Where are you from? I am from Mexico.); A1+ 3.7 asks what language they speak. It adds no new grammar relationship: What + language opens A1 4.8's do you question (What language do you speak?), and speak takes A1+ 1.2's -s (Diego speaks Spanish.). Spanish, the A1 nationality, is also the language. A1 3.7-3.8's country photos, with their flags, show where people speak Spanish or English; the cast's languages follow their A1 countries (Ana Mexican, Luis American, Sofia Canadian, Diego Spanish) and are always said, never guessed from a picture. The 3.1 newcomer asks Ana and Diego.
lesson.prerequisite: A1 3.7-3.8 countries and nationalities; A1 4.8 Do you …?; A1 1.11 people; A1+ 1.2 the he/she -s; A1+ 3.1 the café newcomer; A1+ 3.2 we.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say speak with a long ee and English as ING-glish, two syllables. Do not require native-like speed.
